name: Penelope Tang
occupation: Former volunteer and paid shop worker
life: “I still remember delivering lunch to avoid coming home too early.” Saturday often includes a stop at the market by Market Flats, where Penelope often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I volunteered because the route got me out of a miserable house. I can't give my new wages away.
appearance: Penelope has a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears, two dimples that appear only with a full smile, and a favorite piece of clothing, a charcoal zip cardigan. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Penelope draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Penelope carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To start the paid job with a clean handover of deliveries.
family: Nina Arendt is Penelope’s older cousin. Penelope asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Nina remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The empty chair on nights*, Nina says, “I trained her and missed every sign she was working past her limit.”
connections: Jonas Osborne. The former volunteer tells a regular who really paid for delivery time. Also in the story is Erin Roche (deli colleague).

reactions.situation: A housebound customer cannot afford the delivery fee
reactions.response: Penelope asks whether combining a delivery with a willing neighbor would help.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Penelope asks the counter staff for a receipt so its return can be traced even after their shift changes.

reactions.response: Penelope offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
